This script compares the two groups at baseline, fits the propensity score model and computes the inverse probability of treatment weights. It adds `propensity_score` and `ipw` to `patients` for [8. Outcomes](08_outcomes.qmd).

## Propensity model

The covariates are those listed in the paper. In Stata, `Gender` was the numbered category made by `encode` (1 = F, 2 = M) entered as a number, which is the same model as a male indicator. Patients missing any covariate, for example with no viral load before ART, get no score and so no weight, and drop out of the weighted analyses, as they did in Stata.

One difference to know about: if a category predicts the regimen perfectly (every patient in it started the STR, say), Stata's `logistic` drops that category and its patients with a note, while `glm()` keeps them and gives probabilities close to 0 or 1, and so very large weights. Check the fitted model for this before using the weights.

```{r}
#| label: fit-propensity-model
#| eval: false
```

## Weights

Stata:

```stata
predict PropensityScore, p
generate IPW=(InitialRegimenSTR/PropensityScore)+(1-InitialRegimenSTR)/(1-PropensityScore)
```

The formula picks 1/p for STR patients and 1/(1-p) for the others; `if_else()` says so directly. These are average-treatment-effect weights.

```{r}
#| label: compute-weights
#| eval: false
```
